name: TX-18
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +29 point partisan lean
Incumbent Menefee running with large fundraising and outside support
Republican opponent has raised essentially nothing
model.rationale: TX-18's +29 Democratic lean, Menefee's incumbency and roughly $3.6 million raised against an underfunded Republican challenger make this a Safe D race, consistent with markets pricing Democrats near 96%.
model.watch: A major late scandal or unexpected outside spending surge could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-18 is a heavily Democratic Houston-area seat with a +29 point partisan lean. Incumbent Christian Menefee, a Democrat, is running for a full term and has raised about $3.6 million, with roughly $7 million in outside support and no outside opposition spending. Republican Ronald Whitfield has shown no meaningful fundraising or campaign infrastructure.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic margin of roughly 29 points.
